topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Larger SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas increase radiation efficiency but lead to higher insertion loss due to longer SIW lengths, reducing overall efficiency. The physical footprint increases, impacting spacecraft design and cost. Material properties become increasingly critical as SIW arrays scale, impacting the design and performance of large arrays. Inaccurate material properties used in the design stage contribute to discrepancies between simulated and measured gains. Optimizing the frequency response is crucial for maintaining high efficiency for larger arrays.
reference_context: A wideband high-gain high-efficiency hybrid-integrated plate array antenna for V-band inter-satellite links was presented, featuring microstrip patches, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), and waveguide power dividers. The radiation efficiency of SIW arrays with different sizes was compared by experiment, showing a drastic drop from 70% to 27.5% as the array size increased from 16x16 to 32x32.
